words.childMeaning: A soft pet animal that says miaow and has long whiskers.
practiceSentences: A little cat sits by the door.
Whose cat is this, Amal?
That grey cat is mine!
My cat likes warm milk.
The cat runs after a small bug.

words.childMeaning: A long piece of wood you hold to hit a ball.
practiceSentences: Adam holds the bat with two hands.
Where is my bat, Mum?
That bat is too big for me!
Amal picks up the bat and smiles.
We keep the bat by the door.

words.childMeaning: Something you wear on your head to keep warm or shady.
practiceSentences: Adam puts on his blue hat.
Where is my sun hat?
Here is your hat, Amal.
My hat keeps my head warm.
The hat hangs on a hook.

words.childMeaning: A flat mat you put on the floor to sit or stand on.
practiceSentences: Grandma was making a mat from soft grass.
My mat is by the door.
Is this your mat, Adam?
What a soft mat this is!
Amal sits on her mat to read.

words.childMeaning: A drawing that shows you where places are.
practiceSentences: The map shows every street in our town.
Can you find the ferry on this map?
“Turn the map the right way up,” laughed Adam.
I keep a small map in my school bag.
A red star on the map marks the library.

words.childMeaning: A small word that means you are able to do something.
practiceSentences: Amal can jump very high.
Can you tie your shoes?
Yes, I can do it!
I can read this little book.
Birds can fly in the sky.

words.childMeaning: A man is a grown-up male person.
practiceSentences: A kind man helped Amal find her mum.
Do you know that man over there?
Look, Adam, the man is playing a drum!
The man smiled and waved at us.
A kind man was selling sweet mangoes.

words.childMeaning: Ran means moved fast on your legs, and it already happened.
practiceSentences: Adam ran across the field.
Who ran the fastest today?
Adam ran fast and laughed!
Amal ran home before tea time.
Amal ran outside to play.

words.childMeaning: A big car with lots of room for boxes or people.
practiceSentences: A white van stops at our gate.
Is the school van here yet?
Yes, the van is waiting!
I ride in the van every morning.
The van carries big boxes inside.

words.childMeaning: A fan spins round and round to make cool air.
practiceSentences: The fan is on above our heads.
Can you feel the fan, Adam?
That fan spins so fast!
Grandma turns the fan on.
Our fan is white and quiet.

words.childMeaning: We say an before a word that starts with an a, e, i, o or u sound.
practiceSentences: I have an apple in my bag.
Is that an egg, Mum?
What an old book this is!
Adam draws an orange sun.
She waited an hour for Grandma.

words.childMeaning: This word tells you where something is, or when it happens.
practiceSentences: Amal is at school today.
Are you at home, Adam?
Look at the big red bus!
We meet at the gate.
Grandma waits at the door.

words.childMeaning: We use am with I to say who we are or how we feel.
practiceSentences: I am six years old.
Am I in your class?
I am so happy today!
I am ready to read.
I am Amal, and this is Adam.

words.childMeaning: A tap lets water come out when you turn it.
practiceSentences: The tap is by the door.
Can you turn the tap off, Adam?
That tap drips all day!
Amal fills her cup at the tap.
Grandma washes the plates at the tap.

words.childMeaning: A soft hat with a flat part at the front to keep the sun off.
practiceSentences: My cap is blue and white.
Where is your cap, Amal?
What a smart cap that is!
Adam puts his cap on his head.
Grandma keeps her cap by the door.

words.childMeaning: A bag is something you carry your things in.
practiceSentences: My bag is by the desk.
Is this your bag, Adam?
What a heavy bag this is!
Amal packs her bag every morning.
Mum carries a big bag to the market.

words.childMeaning: A small label on something that shows whose it is.
practiceSentences: My bag has a red tag.
Whose name is on this tag?
That tag has fallen off!
Adam writes his name on the tag.
Every coat has a tag inside.

words.childMeaning: Sweet, sticky food made from fruit. We spread it on bread.
practiceSentences: Amal puts jam on her toast.
Do you like strawberry jam?
Yes, jam is my favourite!
My jam is sweet and red.
The jam jar is on the shelf.

words.childMeaning: The place where you live with your family.
practiceSentences: We walk home after school.
Is Grandma at home today?
What a warm home this is!
Amal runs home to tell Mum.
My home is near the school.

words.childMeaning: A house is the building where a family lives.
practiceSentences: Amal ran to Grandma's house.
Whose house is this, Amal?
What a big house it is!
The house was full of laughter.
Near her house there was a deep well.

words.childMeaning: A space inside a house with walls, a floor and a door.
practiceSentences: My room is small and tidy.
Which room is yours, Adam?
What a bright room this is!
Grandma sits in the front room.
We eat together in this room.

words.childMeaning: The part of a room you open to go in or out.
practiceSentences: The door is open for us.
Can you close the door, Adam?
What a big blue door that is!
Amal knocks on the door.
Grandma waits by the door.

words.childMeaning: A window is an opening in a wall that lets in light.
practiceSentences: Adam looked out of the window.
Is the window open or closed?
Look, a bird is at the window!
Amal cleaned the window with a cloth.
Amal found a seat by the window.

words.childMeaning: A seat with a back and four legs for one person.
practiceSentences: Adam pushes in his chair.
May I take this chair?
Yes, that chair is free.
My chair is next to the window.
The teacher's chair is by the whiteboard.

words.childMeaning: A flat top with legs where we work or eat.
practiceSentences: Our books sit on the table.
Is your lunchbox on the table?
Yes, it is on the table!
I write at my little table.
We eat dinner at the table.

words.childMeaning: The place where children go to learn and play.
practiceSentences: My school starts at eight o'clock.
Do you like your new school?
Adam, I love our school!
I ride the bus to school.
Our school is near the park.

words.childMeaning: All the children who learn together with one teacher.
practiceSentences: My class has twenty children.
Which class are you in, Amal?
What a busy class we are!
Our class reads together after break.
I like my class very much.

words.childMeaning: Pages joined together with stories, pictures or words to read.
practiceSentences: Amal opens her new book.
Which book do you like best?
This book is about a kind lion!
I keep my book in my bag.
The teacher reads a book to us.

words.childMeaning: A thin wooden stick we write and draw with.
practiceSentences: Adam writes with a grey pencil.
Can I borrow your pencil?
Yes, here is my pencil.
My pencil is sharp and long.
The pencil is inside the box.

words.childMeaning: A table where you sit to read and write at school.
practiceSentences: My desk is by the window.
Is this your desk, Adam?
What a tidy desk that is!
Amal puts her book on the desk.
We share one desk in our class.

words.childMeaning: A small word we use before one thing, like 'a hat'.
practiceSentences: Adam has a big blue ball.
Would you like a pencil?
Yes, please give me a pencil.
I drew a cat in my book.
We sit on a soft mat.

words.childMeaning: A small word we put before a naming word, like 'the cat'.
practiceSentences: The teacher opens the book.
Where is the pencil?
The pencil is here, Adam!
I read the story to my sister.
The children sit on the mat.

words.childMeaning: A small word that tells us about now, like 'she is happy'.
practiceSentences: The sun is bright today.
Where is your lunchbox?
It is under the table!
My name is Amal.
This book is about a goat.

words.childMeaning: A small word we use instead of naming a thing again.
practiceSentences: It is raining outside today.
Where did you put it?
I put it in my bag.
My cat is small and it purrs.
It is time for our lesson.

words.childMeaning: Inside something else, with walls or sides all around it.
practiceSentences: The spider waits in the middle of its web.
Who is hiding in the tall grass?
“The cricket is in my pocket,” laughed Amal.
I keep my bug book in my school bag.
Bees sleep in the hive when night comes.

words.childMeaning: A small word you use when you talk about yourself.
practiceSentences: I like reading with my teacher.
May I sit here, please?
Yes, I can help you!
I say bismillah before I eat.
Every morning I walk to school.

words.childMeaning: This word means the person I am talking to.
practiceSentences: You are in my class.
How are you today, Adam?
What a kind friend you are!
Are you ready to read?
You can sit next to me.

words.childMeaning: This word joins two things together.
practiceSentences: Mum and Grandma are at home.
Do you want a book and a pencil?
What a big cat and a small cat!
I have a bag and a cap.
We sing and clap together.

words.childMeaning: This word shows where someone or something is going.
practiceSentences: I go to school with Adam.
Are you going to the market?
Come to the door, please!
Grandma walks to the shop.
Give the book to your teacher.

words.childMeaning: The number 1. It means just a single thing.
practiceSentences: Adam has one little brother.
May I have one grape?
Yes, take one grape.
I can see one bright moon.
One duck swims in the pond.

words.childMeaning: Very small in size, so it fits in your hand.
practiceSentences: My little brother rides with me.
Can I have a little help?
Adam, that boat is little!
I keep my coins in a little box.
A little chick follows the hen.

words.childMeaning: This word means not any. It is the opposite of yes.
practiceSentences: No, that bag is not mine.
There is no milk left.
No rain came today.
Is there no bread, Mum?
No! Do not touch the hot pot.

words.childMeaning: Yes is the word we use to agree with something.
practiceSentences: Yes, I would like to play.
Adam, will you say yes?
Yes! I love school!
Amal nodded and said yes.
Yes, of course.

words.childMeaning: This word means in this place, close to you.
practiceSentences: The bus stops right here.
Is my bag here or there?
Come here, we are ready!
I put my shoes here every day.
Here is the road we must cross.

words.childMeaning: Something a hen lays that we can cook and eat.
practiceSentences: The egg is warm in the nest.
Would you like an egg for breakfast?
Amal, I found one more egg!
I carry the egg very carefully.
A chick comes out of the egg.

words.childMeaning: A female farm bird that lays eggs for us.
practiceSentences: The hen sits in her warm nest.
Where is the little brown hen?
Amal, our hen laid two eggs!
I collect eggs from our hen.
A hen clucks when she is happy.

words.childMeaning: A bed is where you lie down and sleep.
practiceSentences: the baby sleeps in a small bed.
Is it time for bed?
Jump into bed quickly!
Amal made her bed this morning.
My bed is soft and warm.

words.childMeaning: A thin tool with ink that we write with.
practiceSentences: Teacher writes with a black pen.
Where is my new pen?
Your pen is on the desk.
My pen writes in blue ink.
The pen rolls off the table.

words.childMeaning: Covered with water, the way your coat feels after rain.
practiceSentences: The wet path shines after the rain.
Why is your school bag wet?
Careful, the floor is still wet!
I dry my wet hands on a towel.
Wet grass tickles Adam's bare feet.

words.childMeaning: The number 10. It is how many fingers you have.
practiceSentences: We count to ten together.
Can you count to ten?
Yes, I can count to ten!
I have ten little toes.
Ten birds sit on the roof.

words.childMeaning: A net is made of string with holes in it, for catching things.
practiceSentences: The net is full of fish.
Can you hold the net, Adam?
What a big net that is!
Amal caught the ball in the net.
Grandma mends the net by the door.

words.childMeaning: A pet is an animal you keep at home and look after.
practiceSentences: My pet is a small brown hen.
Do you have a pet, Adam?
What a happy pet she is!
Amal feeds her pet every day.
A cat can be a good pet.

words.childMeaning: Men means more than one man.
practiceSentences: Two men carried the big box.
Are those men your uncles?
The men sang together!
Three men waited at the gate.
The men helped us with our bags.

words.childMeaning: A part that rings to tell people you are coming.
practiceSentences: My bicycle has a silver bell.
Did you ring the bell?
Amal, ring your bell for me!
I ring my bell before I turn.
The school bell tells us to line up.

words.childMeaning: Tell means to say something to another person using words.
practiceSentences: Adam likes to tell funny stories.
Can you tell me your name?
Tell us what you learned today!
Amal will tell her mum about school.
Tell Mum what you made today.

words.childMeaning: A young male child, like a brother or a school friend.
practiceSentences: That boy is called Adam.
Which boy is your brother?
The tall boy is my brother!
I sit beside a friendly boy.
One boy is drawing a kite.

words.childMeaning: A young female child, like a sister or a school friend.
practiceSentences: That girl is called Amal.
Is the girl in your class?
Yes, the girl sits near me!
I play with a kind girl.
One girl is feeding the ducks.

words.childMeaning: A child is a young person who is not grown up yet.
practiceSentences: Every child in my class can read.
Is that child your sister?
What a kind child she is!
One child sat by the window.
Each child has a name tag.

words.childMeaning: A very young child who cannot walk or talk yet.
practiceSentences: The baby laughs at the cat.
Is the baby asleep?
Yes, the baby is sleeping!
I hold my baby brother gently.
The baby drinks warm milk.

words.childMeaning: The woman who has you as her child and cares for you.
practiceSentences: Amal's mother works at the shop.
Where is your mother?
My mother is in the kitchen.
I help my mother every day.
A mother looks after her children.

words.childMeaning: The man who has you as his child and cares for you.
practiceSentences: Adam's father works in a shop.
Where does your father work?
My father works at the hospital.
I walk to the library with my father.
A father looks after his family.

words.childMeaning: Another word for mother that we use at home.
practiceSentences: Adam hugs his mum.
Is your mum at home?
Yes, my mum is here!
I love my mum very much.
Mum reads to us at bedtime.

words.childMeaning: Another word for father that we use at home.
practiceSentences: Dad helps me with my reading.
Is your dad home yet?
Yes, my dad just came home!
I play football with my dad.
Dad cooks rice for dinner.

words.childMeaning: A girl who has the same mother or father as you.
practiceSentences: Amal has one little sister.
How old is your sister?
My sister is three today!
I share my books with my sister.
My big sister helps me tidy up.

words.childMeaning: A boy who has the same mother or father as you.
practiceSentences: Adam has a baby brother.
Does your brother go to school?
Yes, my brother is in Grade 3!
I read to my little brother.
My brother helps dad wash the van.

words.childMeaning: Your grandma is the mother of your mum or your dad.
practiceSentences: Amal's grandma was there.
Her grandma kept animals there.
Is your grandma at home, Adam?
My grandma tells the best stories.
She ran and gave Grandma a big hug.

words.childMeaning: Your grandpa is the father of your mum or your dad.
practiceSentences: Amal sat with her grandpa.
Is your grandpa at home, Adam?
What a kind grandpa you have!
My grandpa walks to the shop each day.
Grandpa hugged him tightly.

words.childMeaning: The people you live with and love, like parents and children.
practiceSentences: Our family visits grandma on Friday.
How big is your family?
My family has five people!
I love my family very much.
The whole family helps at the school fair.

words.childMeaning: Someone you like, play with and are kind to.
practiceSentences: Amal helps her friend tidy up.
Who is your best friend?
Amal is my friend!
I share my snack with a friend.
A good friend is always kind.

words.childMeaning: A grown-up who helps you learn new things at school.
practiceSentences: Our teacher smiles every morning.
May I ask the teacher?
Yes, the teacher is by the door.
I show my work to my teacher.
The teacher reads us a lovely story.

words.childMeaning: A small word that shows something is above and touching, like 'on the table'.
practiceSentences: The cat sits on the mat.
Is your bag on the table?
Yes, it is on the table!
I put my lunchbox on the shelf.
The bird lands on the roof.

words.childMeaning: This word makes a sentence mean the opposite.
practiceSentences: Amal did not rush.
The plants did not grow.
We must not waste water.
But her mat was not neat.
"Do not be sad," said Adam.

words.childMeaning: Towards a higher place, like the sky above your head.
practiceSentences: The bird flies up to the tree.
Can you jump up high?
Amal, look up at the moon!
I walk up the hill slowly.
The lift takes us up.

words.childMeaning: This word means me and the people with me.
practiceSentences: Come and sit with us, Adam.
Will you read to us, Mum?
Grandma made lunch for us!
The teacher gave us new books.
Let us count the grapes together.

words.childMeaning: To look at something and know it with your eyes.
practiceSentences: We see many birds in the tree.
What can you see, Adam?
I see two green frogs!
I see my friend at the gate.
Owls can see well at night.

words.childMeaning: The number 2. It means one more than one.
practiceSentences: Amal has two red crayons.
Can you clap two times?
Yes, I clapped two times!
I have two small feet.
Two birds sit in the tree.

words.childMeaning: Good means nice, kind, or done well.
practiceSentences: That was a good story, Mum.
Are you good at running, Adam?
What a good friend you are!
Amal had a good day at school.
Good morning, everyone!

words.childMeaning: All means every one of them, with none left out.
practiceSentences: I love my family best of all.
It drove all the way to the sea.
Last of all, they came to the library.
All the children sat down.
Amal ate all her rice.

words.childMeaning: This word means in that place, away from you.
practiceSentences: My school is just there.
Who is standing over there?
Look, there is the bus stop!
I left my coat there yesterday.
There are many shops on this road.

words.childMeaning: Said means spoke. It already happened.
practiceSentences: "Come, Amal," said her mum.
"Yes, please," said Grandma.
"I love Saturday," said Amal.
"I love you, Grandma," said Amal.
"Let us count the grapes," said Grandpa.

words.childMeaning: This word shows where someone or something started.
practiceSentences: She smelled hot spices from a big pot.
Grandma was making a mat from soft grass.
Her big brother Adam waved from the gate.
Amal walked home from school.
This letter is from my teacher.

words.childMeaning: Out means away from the inside of something.
practiceSentences: Amal ran out to play.
Can you take the bin out?
The cat jumped out of the box!
We go out after lunch.
Adam looked out of the window.

words.childMeaning: This word asks about the time something happens.
practiceSentences: When do we go home?
When is your birthday, Adam?
Tell me when you are ready!
Amal smiles when she sees Grandma.
We read when the bell rings.

words.childMeaning: Large in size, taking up lots of space.
practiceSentences: My school bag is too big.
Is that plane big or small?
Amal, that bus is big!
I drew a big red tractor.
A big boat carries many people.

words.childMeaning: A pink farm animal with a curly tail and flat nose.
practiceSentences: The pig has a short curly tail.
Can you see the pig in the mud?
Amal, that pig is very pink!
I look at the pig from the gate.
Muslims do not eat meat from a pig.

words.childMeaning: The number 6. It comes after five and before seven.
practiceSentences: Amal has six new crayons.
Are there six children here?
Yes, I count six children!
I have six books at home.
Six birds sit on the wall.

words.childMeaning: Dig means to make a hole in the ground.
practiceSentences: Adam likes to dig in the sand.
Can we dig here, Mum?
Dig a little deeper!
Amal will dig a hole for the seed.
The hen digs in the soft soil.

words.childMeaning: To knock something with your hand or with a bat.
practiceSentences: Adam can hit the ball far.
Can you hit the ball, Adam?
Yes, I will hit it gently!
I hit the ball with my bat.
We must never hit our friends.

words.childMeaning: A bit means a small amount of something.
practiceSentences: Amal ate a bit of bread.
Can I have a bit, please?
Wait a bit longer!
Adam gave a bit of his cake to Amal.
There is a bit of rice left.

words.childMeaning: A pin is a small thin piece of metal with a sharp point.
practiceSentences: Mum used a pin to hold the cloth.
Where is the pin, Grandma?
That pin is very sharp!
Amal pinned her picture to the board.
Keep the pin in the tin.

words.childMeaning: A fin is the flat part on a fish that helps it swim.
practiceSentences: The fish moved its fin slowly.
Can you see the fin, Adam?
What a big fin that fish has!
A fish uses its fin to turn.
Amal drew a fin on her fish.

words.childMeaning: A tin is a metal box that keeps food fresh.
practiceSentences: The rice is in the big tin.
Can you open this tin, Mum?
What a shiny tin that is!
Grandma keeps her tea in a tin.
Put the lid back on the tin.

words.childMeaning: Your lips are the soft edges of your mouth.
practiceSentences: Amal bit her lip and thought hard.
Can you touch your lip?
My lip feels dry today!
Adam wiped his lip with a cloth.
A smile starts at your lips.

words.childMeaning: Dip means to put something into water or food for a moment.
practiceSentences: Amal likes to dip her bread in the soup.
Do you dip your biscuit in tea?
Dip your brush in the water!
Adam dipped one toe in the sea.
We dip the cloth and then wash.

words.childMeaning: To take hold of something moving in the air.
practiceSentences: Adam can catch the big ball.
Can you catch this, Amal?
Yes, I can catch it!
I catch the ball with both hands.
Cats catch bugs in the garden.

words.childMeaning: To hit your hands together to make a sound.
practiceSentences: We clap when the story ends.
Can you clap three times?
Yes, I can clap fast!
I clap my hands together.
We clap for Adam's good reading.

words.childMeaning: To push off the ground with both feet.
practiceSentences: Amal can jump very high.
Can you jump ten times?
Yes, watch me jump!
I jump over the long rope.
Frogs jump out of the pond.

words.childMeaning: Kick means to hit something with your foot.
practiceSentences: Adam can kick the ball very far.
Can you kick it to me?
What a strong kick that was!
Amal kicked the ball to Adam.
We kick the ball at break time.

words.childMeaning: To make a happy sound when something is funny.
practiceSentences: The children laugh at the puppy.
Why did you laugh?
I laugh because it is funny!
I laugh with my little sister.
We all laugh together at dinner.

words.childMeaning: To move your legs very fast, faster than walking.
practiceSentences: The children run across the field.
Can you run to the tree?
Yes, I can run fast!
I run home after school.
Dogs run faster than people.

words.childMeaning: To sit on something and travel, like a bicycle or horse.
practiceSentences: My friends ride bicycles after school.
Can you ride a horse?
Adam, let us ride together!
I ride the bus with my sister.
We ride slowly along the quiet road.

words.childMeaning: Sit means to rest on a chair or on the floor.
practiceSentences: I can sit on the rug.
Where shall we sit, Adam?
Sit next to me!
Amal likes to sit by the window.
We sit down when the bell rings.

words.childMeaning: To rest with your eyes closed, usually at night.
practiceSentences: the baby falls asleep as soon as the light goes off.
What time do you sleep on a school night?
“A good sleep helps you learn,” said the doctor.
I sleep for ten hours and wake up full of energy.
Cats sleep in the sunny corner of the room.

words.childMeaning: A smile is the happy shape your mouth makes when you are pleased.
practiceSentences: Adam had a smile on his face.
Can you give me a smile, Amal?
What a lovely smile, Amal!
Her smile made everyone feel happy.
Amal smiled a big smile.

words.childMeaning: To be up on your feet, and not sitting down.
practiceSentences: Adam stands beside the door and waits for his class.
How long can you stand on one foot?
“Stand tall and take a deep breath,” said the teacher.
I stand up when my grandma comes into the room.
The runners stand in a line before the race begins.

words.childMeaning: To send something through the air with your hand.
practiceSentences: Amal can throw the ball high.
Can you throw it to me?
Yes, I will throw it now!
I throw my ball in the park.
We throw the ball in the playground.

words.childMeaning: A page is one side of a sheet of paper in a book.
practiceSentences: Amal turned to the next page.
Which page are we on, Adam?
What a colourful page this is!
Read the first page out loud.
My favourite page has a picture of a cat.

words.childMeaning: A word is a group of letters that means something, like cat or run.
practiceSentences: Can you read this word?
Adam learned a new word today.
What a long word that is!
I can spell my favourite word.
Amal wrote one new word in her book.

words.childMeaning: A letter is one of the signs we use to write words, like a or b.
practiceSentences: The first letter of my name is A.
Which letter comes after b?
That letter is hard to write!
Amal traced the letter with her finger.
Every word is made of letters.

words.childMeaning: A picture is a drawing or photo of something.
practiceSentences: Adam painted a picture of his dog.
Can I see your picture?
What a lovely picture!
Amal hung her picture on the wall.
Amal drew a picture of Grandma.

words.childMeaning: A straight tool for drawing lines and measuring things.
practiceSentences: Amal draws a line with her ruler.
Where is your ruler?
My ruler is in the drawer.
I measure my book with a ruler.
The ruler is long and straight.

words.childMeaning: A board is a flat surface on the wall that the teacher writes on.
practiceSentences: The teacher wrote our names on the board.
Can you see the board, Adam?
What a big board that is!
Amal points to a word on the board.
We copy the letters from the board.

words.childMeaning: This word points to something close to you.
practiceSentences: This is my book.
Is this your bag, Adam?
What a lovely day this is!
"This is a special place," said Mum softly.
This cat lives next door.

words.childMeaning: This word points to something further away from you.
practiceSentences: That is Adam's bag.
Do you see that bird?
What a tall tree that is!
That night, Amal looked at the full well.
That book on the shelf is mine.

words.childMeaning: This word means those people or those things.

words.childMeaning: A light colour made from red and white, like a flower.

words.childMeaning: A colour made from red and blue, like a grape.

words.childMeaning: The colour of soil, tree trunks and warm bread.

words.childMeaning: A round shape with no corners, like the sun.

words.childMeaning: Something short is not very long or tall.
practiceSentences: My hair is short and curly.
Is this rope short or long?
Amal, your ruler is short!
I take short steps beside Dad.
A short walk takes five minutes.

words.childMeaning: Bad means not good.
practiceSentences: The milk had gone bad.
Was the storm very bad, Mum?
That was a bad fall!
Amal had a bad cough all week.
It is bad to drop litter.

words.childMeaning: Something cold feels chilly, like ice or snow.
practiceSentences: My hands are cold outside.
Is your drink cold enough?
Amal, my feet are cold!
I wear a jacket on cold days.
Cold wind blows across the field.

words.childMeaning: Moving very quickly, so you get there in no time.
practiceSentences: The helicopter flies fast above us.
Can you run fast?
Amal, that car is fast!
I finish my work fast.
A fast bus reaches town quickly.

words.childMeaning: Moving gently without hurrying, so you take a long time.
practiceSentences: The old bus is quite slow.
Why is the traffic so slow?
Adam, be slow near the school gate!
I like the slow ride home.
A slow boat drifts down the river.

words.childMeaning: With no dirt on it, washed and fresh.
practiceSentences: Clean water is safe to drink.
Is your face clean for dinner?
Well done, your desk looks clean!
I clean my teeth every morning.
We keep the hall floor clean.

words.childMeaning: Covered with mud, dust or marks, needing a wash.
practiceSentences: The dirty plates go in the sink.
Why are your shoes so dirty?
Oh dear, your shirt is dirty!
I wash my dirty hands with soap.
Dirty water is not safe to drink.

words.childMeaning: Something soft feels gentle and nice to touch.
practiceSentences: My blanket is warm and soft.
Is this wool soft or rough?
Adam, the chick is so soft!
I like my soft pillow.
Soft sand feels lovely under our feet.

words.childMeaning: Something hard does not bend when you press it.
practiceSentences: My desk is very hard.
Is the bread hard or soft?
Amal, this nut is too hard!
I knock on the hard door.
Hard ice melts in the warm sun.

words.childMeaning: A loud sound feels very big in your ears.
practiceSentences: My baby brother has a loud cry.
Was the thunder very loud?
Adam, that goose is loud!
I do not like loud noises.
Loud voices are not kind in class.

words.childMeaning: A quiet sound is very small and soft.
practiceSentences: My little kitten is very quiet.
Can you be quiet, please?
Adam, the library is quiet now!
I read in a quiet corner.
Quiet feet do not wake the baby.

words.childMeaning: Full means there is no more room inside.
practiceSentences: It was bumpy and full of holes.
Up came the pot, full and heavy.
That night, Amal looked at the full well.
Is your cup full, Adam?
The bus was full of people.

words.childMeaning: Empty means a container has nothing inside it at all.
practiceSentences: Is the bottle empty?
Amal found an empty jug.
The empty box was very light.
Adam looked inside the empty pot.
They carried an empty pot.

words.childMeaning: Having no water on it at all, like sand in sunshine.
practiceSentences: The hot sun makes the clothes dry.
Are your shoes dry now?
Yes, my hair is dry already!
I keep my books in a dry place.
Dry sand slips through Amal's fingers.

words.childMeaning: Funny means something that makes you laugh or smile.
practiceSentences: Adam told a funny story.
Is this book funny, Amal?
What a funny little goat!
The monkey made a funny face.
We laughed at her funny song.

words.childMeaning: Beautiful means very pretty and lovely to look at.
practiceSentences: Amal's finished mat was beautiful.
Is that a beautiful flower, Amal?
Wow, your painting is beautiful, Adam!
Grandma has a beautiful garden.
"It is beautiful," said Amal.

words.childMeaning: Happy means you feel good and want to smile.
practiceSentences: Adam is happy today.
Are you happy to see your friends?
How happy Amal looked!
A happy song filled the classroom.
Amal was happy to see Grandma.

words.childMeaning: Sad means you feel unhappy, like when something upsets you.
practiceSentences: Why do you look so sad?
Amal was sad to leave the park.
The sad puppy sat by the door.
Do not be sad, we can fix it!
But Adam looked sad.

words.childMeaning: Kind means you are gentle and helpful to other people.
practiceSentences: Adam is kind to his friends.
Was the teacher kind to you?
How kind of Amal to help!
A kind boy shared his pencil.
A kind man was selling sweet mangoes.

words.childMeaning: First means coming before every other one.
practiceSentences: Adam raised his hand first.
Who was first in the line?
Amal was first to say hello!
This is the first page of my book.
She called it My First English World.

words.childMeaning: Last means after everything else has happened.
practiceSentences: Who finished last in the race?
Adam, you went last this time!
Last, we washed our hands for dinner.
She ate her fruit last of all.
Last of all, they came to the library.

words.childMeaning: Before means earlier than something else happens.
practiceSentences: Wash your hands before you eat.
Adam woke up before the sun came up.
Amal, come inside before it gets dark!
We fed the cow before we left.
Say hello before you sit down.

words.childMeaning: After means later than something else, or next in time.
practiceSentences: We play after lunch.
What happens after the story?
After the game, everyone cheered!
Grandma rested after her long walk.
After breakfast, the family sat together.

words.childMeaning: Now means at this moment, not later.
practiceSentences: She was happy now.
Now the park was clean and pretty.
"Now we must feed the hens," said Grandma.
Can we go now, Adam?
It is time to read now.

words.childMeaning: Today means this day, the one we are in now.
practiceSentences: Today was Amal's first day at school.
Today, Amal was going to see her grandma.
"Today we will walk around our town," said Mum.
What did you learn today, Adam?
Today is a warm and sunny day.

words.childMeaning: Tomorrow means the day after today.
practiceSentences: We will go to the farm tomorrow.
Will you be here tomorrow, Adam?
Tomorrow is my birthday!
Amal will bring her mat tomorrow.
The bread will be fresh tomorrow.

words.childMeaning: Morning is the early part of the day, soon after you wake up.
practiceSentences: Grandma makes tea every morning.
Is it morning yet, Adam?
What a lovely morning it is!
The family ate breakfast in the morning.
It was Saturday morning.

words.childMeaning: The afternoon is the time of day between midday and evening.
practiceSentences: The sun was hot in the afternoon.
Do you rest in the afternoon?
Amal, it is already afternoon!
We visited Grandma one warm afternoon.
It was a warm afternoon in the village.

words.childMeaning: The part of the day before night, when the sun sets.
practiceSentences: In the evening the sun sinks low behind the hills.
What do you like doing in the evening?
“Sit with me this evening,” said Grandma.
I read my book every evening before bed.
The evening light turned the clouds pink and gold.

words.childMeaning: Night is the time of day when it is dark outside.
practiceSentences: Amal read a book at night.
What did you do last night?
What a lovely night!
Adam slept well that night.
That night, Amal looked at the full well.

words.childMeaning: Zero is the number 0. It means none at all.
practiceSentences: There were zero hens in the yard.
Can you write a zero, Adam?
Zero means we have none!
Amal counted from zero to ten.
The score was two to zero.

words.childMeaning: The number 3. It comes after two and before four.
practiceSentences: There are three eggs in the nest.
Can you jump three times?
Yes, watch me jump three times!
I have three books in my bag.
Three children are drawing quietly.

words.childMeaning: The number 4. It comes after three and before five.
practiceSentences: The chair has four legs.
Are there four apples here?
Yes, I count four apples!
I have four crayons in my box.
Four ducks swim on the pond.

words.childMeaning: The number 5. It is how many fingers are on one hand.
practiceSentences: My hand has five fingers.
Can you count to five?
Yes, five is easy!
I am five years old.
Five grapes are in my lunchbox.

words.childMeaning: The number 7. It comes after six and before eight.
practiceSentences: The rainbow shows seven colours.
Can you count seven stars?
Yes, I found seven stars!
I have seven small stickers.
Seven ducks swim in a line.

words.childMeaning: The number 8. It comes after seven and before nine.
practiceSentences: Adam counts eight red apples.
Are there eight chairs?
Yes, we have eight chairs!
I can hop eight times.
Eight bees fly near the flower.

words.childMeaning: The number 9. It comes after eight and before ten.
practiceSentences: The clock says nine o'clock.
Can you write the number nine?
Yes, I can write nine!
I have nine grapes left.
Nine children sit on the mat.

words.childMeaning: Angry means you feel cross about something.
practiceSentences: Adam was angry when he lost his bat.
Are you angry with me, Amal?
The angry goat stamped its foot!
She felt angry but stayed calm.
It is fine to feel angry sometimes.

words.childMeaning: Afraid means you feel scared of something.
practiceSentences: Amal was afraid of the dark.
Are you afraid of the big dog?
Do not be afraid, I am here!
The chick was afraid of the noise.
He was afraid to speak in front of the class.

words.childMeaning: Tired means you need to rest or sleep.
practiceSentences: She was tired, but she was happy.
Are you tired, Adam?
I am so tired tonight!
The goats were tired after the walk.
Amal felt tired and went to bed.

words.childMeaning: Excited means you feel very happy about something coming soon.
practiceSentences: Amal was excited about her birthday.
Are you excited to see the farm?
How excited the children were!
Adam felt excited before the game.
We are excited to read the new book.

words.childMeaning: Worried means feeling a little afraid that something bad might happen.
practiceSentences: Mum looked worried about the rain.
Are you worried, Amal?
Do not be worried, we can help!
Adam was worried he would be late.
The hen seemed worried about her chicks.

words.childMeaning: Calm means quiet and peaceful, without noise or worry.
practiceSentences: Adam felt calm after the walk.
Is the park calm in the morning?
Stay calm, everything is fine!
Mum spoke in a calm voice.
It was quiet and calm.

words.childMeaning: Please is a kind word we use when we ask for something.
practiceSentences: Please come inside.
"Yes, please," said Grandma.
May I have some water, please?
Please close the door, Adam.
Pass me the spoon, please.

words.childMeaning: We say thank you when someone gives us something or helps us.
practiceSentences: "Thank you for helping," said Amal.
Did you say thank you, Adam?
Thank you for my lovely gift!
We say thank you to our teacher.
Amal said thank you and smiled.

words.childMeaning: Sorry is a word you say when you feel bad about something you did.
practiceSentences: "I am sorry," said Adam.
Are you sorry you shouted?
Sorry, I did not mean to push!
Amal was sorry she broke the cup.
We say sorry when we hurt someone.

words.childMeaning: Hello is a friendly word we say when we meet someone.
practiceSentences: Adam waved and said hello.
Can you say hello to Amal?
Hello, everyone!
The children sang a hello song.
Hello, school!

words.childMeaning: Goodbye is a word you say when someone is leaving.
practiceSentences: We waved goodbye at the bus stop.
Did you say goodbye to Adam?
Amal, wave goodbye to your friend!
Goodbye, we will see you soon.
She said goodbye to Grandma.

words.childMeaning: Welcome is a friendly word you say to greet someone.
practiceSentences: "Welcome, Amal!" said the teacher.
Are new children welcome here?
Welcome to our class!
Grandma made us feel welcome.
We welcome everyone at our school.

words.childMeaning: Share means to give some of what you have to someone else.
practiceSentences: Amal will share her bread.
Can you share the pencils, Adam?
Share the fruit with your friends!
We share our books in class.
It is kind to share.

words.childMeaning: To do something kind that makes things easier for someone.
practiceSentences: We help mum lay the table.
Can you help me, please?
Yes, I can help you!
I help my sister tidy up.
Good friends help each other.

words.childMeaning: Fair means everyone gets the same and nobody is left out.
practiceSentences: It is fair to take turns.
Is that fair, Adam?
That is not fair!
Amal shared the fruit in a fair way.
A fair game means nobody cheats.

words.childMeaning: Into means going to the inside of something.
practiceSentences: The ball went into a big tree.
Put the rice into the pot, please.
Jump into bed quickly!
Amal walked into the classroom.
The cat ran into the garden.

words.childMeaning: This word asks about a place.
practiceSentences: Where is my bag?
Where do you live, Adam?
Tell me where you found it!
Amal asked where the well was.
Where shall we sit today?

words.childMeaning: Should tells you what is the right thing to do.
practiceSentences: We should wash our hands.
Should I bring my book, Adam?
You should say thank you!
Amal knew she should share.
We should be kind to everyone.
